items.title: Christopher "Happy" Goldston Interview, 1962-04-11
items.q: I left Punch. I went with this same band here. Ridgely's Tuxedo. With Baby Eric.

ctx.x: old could go on a dance nowadays. You know that. Yeah. And I played with Punch. A long time. Kid Punch. That was Punch's band here, huh? Yeah, that was Punch's band. Was that after Jesse Jackson

or before? No. After Jesse Jackson, I went at Punch. I stayed at Punch a long time here. I left Punch. I went with this same band here. Ridgely's Tuxedo. With Baby Eric. And after one of the the, this is, this is the band, I started reading it. This band there. And the reason of this band, Ridgely and Celestine, they made up the Tuxedo band years ago. And they stayed together and they had a falling out about one dollar. One dollar. Broke those two men. And so, so, so, so they had a split and Ridgely. And Ridgely…

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: then Happy came with us. Goldstein, his name is. He came with us.

ctx.x: Him and I played together, we is. Very nice color. And, uh, it's the attitude trombone, him and I. Peter Biker, Peter Biker, one of the tronettes. Celestrian was one of the tronettes. When we first started playing, let me get that thing real. When we first started playing, we were with Henry Allen over the river, you see. We all used to play with him, you see. And then we'd pull up and, you know, and I, and we'd take, I met in the other fellas to take the tuxedo bands, you see. I met in the other band. So, he was…

We used Adolph Alexander on the Alto. Was that the young Adolph Alexander or his father? No, no. The young Alexander played with me once, you know, in my history. Yes. He played, coming playing saxophone, Tornet, and playing saxophone.
